patch.value: Mastery check (unfamiliar loss). A sensor's readings contain occasional wild outliers, so you want a robust 'centre' c that minimises L(c) = mean(log(cosh(c - y_i))). Derive the gradient yourself, choose a learning rate you can justify from the loss's curvature, and implement gradient descent. In the docstring, state your learning rate and why it is safe.

Mastery check (unfamiliar loss). A sensor's readings contain occasional wild outliers, so you want a robust 'centre' c that minimises L(c) = mean(log(cosh(c - y_i))). Using the derivative facts given below, derive L'(c) and a bound on L''(c), choose a learning rate you can justify from that curvature bound, and implement gradient descent. In the docstring, state your learning rate and why it is safe.

Return the minimiser of L(c) = mean(log(cosh(c - y_i))) using gradient descent you implement yourself. Stop when |L'(c)| < tol or after max_iter updates. The gradient and the learning-rate choice are part of the task and are not given.

Return the minimiser of L(c) = mean(log(cosh(c - y_i))) using gradient descent you implement yourself. Stop when |L'(c)| < tol or after max_iter updates. Facts you may use (hyperbolic functions are not taught in this track): d/du log(cosh(u)) = tanh(u), and d/du tanh(u) = 1 - tanh(u)^2, which always lies in (0, 1]. Applying these to L, and choosing the learning rate, are part of the task.
